client_brief:
Today's Emberline package, with a reusable segment-card workflow

TODAY'S PRODUCTION: EMBERLINE

We need the dish, promo and segment cards to feel like the same bright, friendly show. This ships daily, so the next person at the desk must be able to repeat the workflow tomorrow.

Start by resolving the two house-colour values in our notes and explaining the choice. The plate edge should be checked on that chosen colour, not only on white.

Dish plate and thumbnail
Today's dish isolated and set on the show's chosen house colour with nothing behind it, the rim holding where the plate meets the cloth when inspected on that colour rather than against white, plus the thumbnail crop cut from it. The house colour decision between the two values in the client's own notes is made and justified rather than picked.

Short promo
A deliberate 4-second-or-shorter edit assembled from the 1 supplied short clip using an explicit timeline, plus one platform reframe and three checked poster frames. Source time ranges must come from motion_source_metadata.json and a task-specific edit decision list. The supplied video files contain no audio streams; use a separate supplied WAV only where one exists and never infer dialogue from silent footage.

Matched day frames
Eight key frames shot across seven hours of moving daylight brought to one show white point, one brightness and one warmth, plus one licensed establishing frame brought into the same world, all at or below their source pixel dimensions. Delivered with a per-frame parameter log recording what was applied and why that frame differed. This is one set with one target, not eight separately pleasing pictures.

Segment-card run
The office's flat card template reverse engineered into a live merge template with every placeholder confirmed present by inspection of the re-exported document, then run against the day's rundown as one card per segment: the printer's deck with page count equal to the segment count in running order and rendered at 300 ppi at trim, each card binding its own segment's still cut from the graded set, the strap and time set from the rundown, plus per segment proofs named from what is actually inside them rather than from the returned order, with the Market Open segment that has no exported frame handled deliberately rather than left as a blank picture well, and the bleed reality of the supplied template stated. Delivered with the live reusable merge template so tomorrow's deck can be run without repeating the reverse engineering.

Editable caption cards
Emberline caption card set as one editable document plus its source: Choose and adapt an Adobe Express template for these supporting pieces, using the supplied brand, approved copy and imagery. Select the strongest fit, replace the template content and correct its background as needed. Supply the editable design link and the requested export, in addition to the commissioned custom production work.

The rundown controls the card count and order. Handle the Market Open image gap deliberately, and leave the template ready for another day's data. The four-second promo remains limited to its supplied clip and any separate audio actually present.

Pack: source_video_files/ (1 measured short file); motion_source_metadata.json; emberline_keyframes/ (8 frames, 3840 x 2160); emberline_dish_hero.jpg (8256 x 5504); emberline_rundown.md; emberline_house_type.md; emberline_bug_grab.png (900 x 600); emberline_card_template.pdf; emberline_cards.csv (9 rows).

Media inventory: 1 video files, 5.042 seconds in total; 0 with embedded audio; 0 separate audio files (0 seconds). These measured sources set the production limits.

Fee range: $5,000-$12,000 fixed
Delivery target: 4 to 6 weeks
Included reviews: Direction approval, first-production proof, and two consolidated revision rounds. New deliverable classes, new source creation, extra records, and client copy changes after approval are quoted separately.

Please deliver a delivery manifest, the editable sources specified above, final exports, a short production and exceptions note, the final edit decision list and measured source metadata and the normalised data and field-mapping record. Account for every supplied file and identify anything used only as reference, superseded or rejected. Stay with approved facts and copy. Do not silently replace weak assets; use only the stated stock or concept allowances, and record omissions, substitutions, reconciliations and material compromises. Keep runtime within measured source duration and the stated cap; do not invent footage or dialogue.

source_provenance.statement: The scenario is synthesized from the repository's laundered Upwork and Freelancer source anchors. It is not represented as a verbatim live listing.
source_provenance.original_anchor: Anchor: the Freelancer.com post quoted in the ledger grounding_note, in which a public facing channel drops fresh promotional footage into a shared drive each afternoon and wants same day tasteful colour correction, a polished screen ready deliverable, the occasional caption line, and a house look the poster describes as lively and accessible, nothing overly corporate, handed back in the daily folder within twenty four hours. The real post named a specific creator's channel and the app they edit in; both are laundered to the coined fictional daily food and craft show Emberline, with the finishing tools named only by what they do. The real post is a maintenance request, which is why it reads thin. The fuller commission that client genuinely needed is the one written here, because the thing they are actually buying is repeatability: the same look has to be reachable tomorrow by someone else, from frames shot hours apart under moving daylight, which turns a colour correction request into a look definition job with a written recipe attached. CONNECTOR_CAPABILITIES_v3 (2026-09-10) makes the rest honest: HTML authoring returns a native editable Express document at mixed canvas sizes so the caption cards can genuinely be retyped tomorrow, licensed Stock supplies the segment nobody shot, and a solid ground knockout produces the thumbnail plate.

price_band_and_audience: Regional daytime lifestyle show, free to watch, products featured at 10 to 30 dollars, mainstream daytime audience skewing 35 to 65. The band is load bearing: at this level the look has to be bright, warm, appetising and legible on a mid range television and a phone, with generous plain type and nothing precious. The same eight frames graded moody and filmic, or styled as a 200 dollar tasting menu with deep shadows, sparse plating and fine type, would be technically excellent and completely wrong for the format, and returning viewers read that drift as the show having changed. Push the other way into hard saturated broadcast punch and the food stops looking edible. A posted job of this shape runs 600 to 1,400 dollars for the first package with a lower daily rate afterwards, which is exactly why the recipe is a deliverable.

brand_identity.sector: Daily food and craft television show on a regional daytime slot, with promos cut for the short video feeds and a same day turnaround.
brand_identity.founded_place_size: On air since 2018, produced in Providence, Rhode Island. A small daily production crew that shoots in the morning, cuts in the afternoon and posts the promo before anyone leaves.
brand_identity.about: Emberline is a bright, friendly daily food and craft show built around one host, a sunny studio kitchen and an accessible dish or make each day. It is free to watch and mainstream in the best sense: warm, unfussy and appetising. Because the promo ships every single day, the brand lives or dies on a look that can be reached again tomorrow by whoever is at the desk.
brand_identity.audience: Mainstream daytime viewers skewing thirty five to sixty five, watching on a mid range television and on their phones. The show is free and the products featured run ten to thirty dollars.
brand_identity.price_positioning: Regional daytime, free to watch, everyday products. The look must be lively, clean and appetising, never moody, filmic or corporate, and never a two hundred dollar tasting menu with deep shadows and fine type. Hard broadcast punch is the other failure: it stops the food looking edible.
brand_identity.typography: A friendly rounded sans for straps and captions with a slightly warmer sans or soft slab for the show name and endboard. Generous, plain and legible on a television and a phone alike. Nothing precious, condensed or editorial.
brand_identity.voice: Upbeat, plain and welcoming, like a host talking to a regular viewer. Example line the brand would write: "Today on Emberline: a white bean and rosemary gratin you can have on the table in under an hour."
brand_identity.brand_assets_status: There is no clean brand kit. The typefaces the on air package used survive only as a previous designer's note written from memory, in loose form. The house colour is recorded twice with two different values, one from the on air graphics package and one from the print kit, with nothing saying which governs, so it must be settled before use.
brand_identity.values: Repeatability and warmth. What the show is actually buying is a look and a written recipe a different editor can run tomorrow, so the brand stays consistent day after day without drift.

assets_supplied.name: emberline_keyframes/ (8 frames, 3840 x 2160)
assets_supplied.kind: Key frames exported off the day's shoot, one per segment, running from roughly nine in the morning to roughly four in the afternoon, each with a grey card held in shot.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "One per segment, with the card in shot for you. They just need to match."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: One frame came off the studio's second body on a different preset, and its card sits inside a shaft of window light and is clipped past recovery, so neutralising to that card swings the whole frame cold and a highlight recovery on it returns a frame that is identical to the one that went in. Another frame's card is only half in shot at the very edge, and one has no card at all because the holder had stepped out, none of which any filename admits.

assets_supplied.name: emberline_dish_hero.jpg (8256 x 5504)
assets_supplied.kind: A single studio still of today's dish, a white bean and rosemary gratin in a white glazed dish set on pale linen, shot on the stills body.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Today's dish. It goes on the thumbnail on its own."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The white glazed dish and the pale linen sit at almost the same value where they meet, so a one call knockout returns a clean, complete, plausible cutout that has quietly bitten into the rim along that edge, and the bite is invisible against white and obvious the moment the plate sits on a saturated ground. The frame is also far larger than anything downstream expects.

assets_supplied.name: emberline_rundown.md
assets_supplied.kind: The day's rundown: segment order, the endboard wording, the strap line, and the two candidate house colour values.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Today's running order and the wording for the endboard."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The rundown lists nine segments while eight frames were exported, and the missing one is the market open the endboard is built around, so the package cannot be completed from the supplied frames alone. The house colour is also stated twice with two different values, one from the on air graphics package and one from the print kit, with nothing saying which governs.

assets_supplied.name: emberline_house_type.md
assets_supplied.kind: A short note from the show's previous designer naming the typefaces the on air package used and roughly how they were set.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "What our graphics used to be set in, as far as we know."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The names are written from memory in mixed case and family form rather than in canonical form, so passing them straight through to a kit build fails outright and takes every valid name in the same request down with it.

assets_supplied.name: emberline_bug_grab.png (900 x 600)
assets_supplied.kind: A low resolution grab of the show's on air ember bug, the little ember mark set beside the Emberline wordmark, lifted off an old broadcast lower third because no vector of it survives.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Our on air bug. We only have it as this screen grab off an old show. The endboard needs it."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: It is a compound lockup, the ember glyph beside the wordmark with a thin underline flourish, so a selection naming the whole bug returns the word and silently drops the ember. The grab is small and JPEG soft with aliased, fringed edges, and the thin flame licks and the tight letter counters that a trace holds at full canvas close into solid blobs at the corner size the endboard bug and the card bug actually reproduce, on the show's cream and coral grounds rather than on white.

assets_supplied.name: emberline_card_template.pdf
assets_supplied.kind: The production office's existing flat template for the show's daily companion card, one card per segment, the file the office already runs the day's deck from.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The card we already print the day's deck on. This is the office's file."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The printed card reads as separate fields, a segment number badge, a name, a time line, a photo panel, a strap and the bug in the corner, but the number, the name and the time are set as one continuous text story in one frame, so offsets have to be computed from the reconstructed story rather than the mapping readout or the time field is silently dropped; the corner bug that reads like a placed logo is a decorative path group and not a picture frame, so the recovered vector has to be placed as a static element rather than bound; and the media box equals the trim with no bleed box, so a press ready with bleed delivery cannot be honoured from it however the render is called.

assets_supplied.name: emberline_cards.csv (9 rows)
assets_supplied.kind: The day's card list, one row per segment: segment number, segment name, approximate time, a short card note, the strap line, and a picture column.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "One row per segment for today's deck. The picture is that segment's frame."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The Market Open row's picture cell is simply blank because that segment was never exported, which no header reveals and the merge will not complain about, and it is the very segment the endboard is built around. The times are written in mixed formats across the rows, and the picture bound to The Make is the window shaft frame whose card cannot be trusted, so the deck inherits a frame that must be neutralised by eye before it can be cut.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Which visible beats in the measured short clips actually cut together without a continuity jump, duplicate action, or missing subject.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: Filenames and source duration do not establish visual continuity. The first assembled proof is the earliest reliable evidence.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Replace or reorder source ranges, shorten the piece, and rebuild the EDL around the strongest continuous action.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A technically valid render feels accidental or implies an action that the source never completes.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether the approved horizontal composition survives the required vertical or square reframe with the subject and essential interface or product detail still visible.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: The crop depends on the actual chosen ranges and subject position inside each rendered frame.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Choose a different source range for the platform version or use fit instead of fill and revise the surrounding design treatment.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: The platform export is correctly sized but loses the person, product, or interface that gives the shot meaning.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether the silent final piece still communicates clearly without implying dialogue, ambience, or music that was never supplied.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: This can be judged only on the final rendered sequence, not from a successful operation response.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Strengthen visual sequencing or approved on-screen copy without fabricating a soundtrack.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: The deliverable relies on absent sound and fails when viewed as supplied.

decision_gates: How much finished runtime the 5.042 measured source seconds can honestly support.
Which source ranges carry complete visible actions rather than attractive but contextless fragments.
Whether the primary edit needs an explicit timeline or qualifies for visually led Quick Cut selection.
Which shots survive the platform reframe without enlargement or loss of the subject.
Whether a separate audio file is usable for the scoped duration, and what must remain silent when no source audio exists.
Which poster frames remain legible and representative at feed size.

verifier_contract.ranking_rule: Rank agents first on host-neutral final artifacts. Report connector completion and normalized process quality as separate dimensions.

artifact_checks.text: The delivery manifest contains every scoped deliverable and no undeclared substitute.
artifact_checks.how: Match the manifest against these exact deliverable names: Emberline dish thumbnail plate; Emberline daily promo spot and vertical; Emberline day frames at one show white point; Emberline today's card deck, one card per segment; Emberline caption card set as one editable document plus its source.

artifact_checks.text: Every supplied input has a recorded disposition.
artifact_checks.how: Compare the input inventory with the manifest and require one of used, reference-only, superseded, or rejected-with-reason for every file.

artifact_checks.text: Every final file is readable and matches its declared format and dimensions.
artifact_checks.how: Open each file with a format-aware parser and compare measured properties with the deliverable manifest.

artifact_checks.text: Every segment in the day's rundown is represented in the delivered package.
artifact_checks.how: Read the rundown's nine listed segments against the delivered set and confirm all nine are represented: the eight exported keyframes plus one licensed establishing frame standing in for Market Open (segment 1), the segment with no exported frame; and confirm the recipe names Market Open as the gap and the licensed establishing frame as how it was closed.

artifact_checks.text: The dish plate sits on a single house colour that the recipe names and justifies, and carries a genuine boundary rather than a rectangle.
artifact_checks.how: Sample the plate's rim edge pixels where it meets the house-colour ground and confirm a genuine anti-aliased plate-to-cloth boundary rather than a straight rectangular cut; confirm the ground is filled with the single chosen house colour, exactly one of #E8623D (on-air graphics) or #E4572E (print kit); and confirm the recipe states which of those two values governs and why.

human_craft_checks.text: The dish cutout holds along the rim where the plate meets the cloth, on the house colour and not against white.
human_craft_checks.how: View the plate at thumbnail size and at full resolution on the chosen colour band.

human_craft_checks.text: The eight frames read as eight moments of one show rather than eight separately pleasing pictures.
human_craft_checks.how: Lay all eight side by side at broadcast scale and judge white point, brightness and warmth as a set, including the frame whose card could not be used.

human_craft_checks.text: The caption cards can be retyped by a producer without breaking, on all three canvases.
human_craft_checks.how: Open the exported document, retype a caption on each canvas and check that nothing reflows off the card.

human_craft_checks.text: The look is lively, clean and appetising for a daytime kitchen show, not moody, filmic or corporate.
human_craft_checks.how: Judge the graded set and the spot against the stated format, band and audience, with the food's appetite appeal as the test.

human_craft_checks.text: The vertical still contains the host and the food, and the host's voice reads clearly over the room.
human_craft_checks.how: Watch the vertical and listen to the spot on a phone speaker as the audience would.

normalized_process_checks.text: Every required connector operation has a normalized execution record.
normalized_process_checks.how: Record the operation name, input asset IDs, output artifact IDs, completion state, retry count, and any exception without relying on host-specific response wording.

normalized_process_checks.text: Material creative decisions are traceable to evidence and alternatives.
normalized_process_checks.how: For each decision gate, record the alternatives compared, the selected option, the evidence used, and the condition that would trigger a revisit.

normalized_process_checks.text: The revision loop closes every failed production or craft gate.
normalized_process_checks.how: Link each failed check to a corrective action, a new artifact version, and the subsequent passing result; unresolved failures must remain declared exceptions.

acceptance_snapshot: The eight frames read as eight moments of one show: one white point, one brightness, one warmth, judged as a set rather than one at a time. A frame that cannot be brought to the set is named rather than shipped at eighty percent.
The dish cutout holds along the rim where the plate meets the cloth, checked on the show's house colour rather than against white, and it sits on one house colour that the note names and justifies.
The caption cards are live editable text across all three canvases in one file the show can open and retype tomorrow, with every line present on every canvas.
Final files open successfully, use unambiguous names, match the stated dimensions and formats, and include editable sources only where the scoped deliverable requires them.
The edit never claims more source duration or source audio than motion_source_metadata.json records, and every delivered time range is traceable to the final EDL.
Every supplied asset is listed in the delivery manifest as used, reference-only, superseded, or rejected with a concrete reason; no input disappears silently.

why_not_vlm: A generated video would replace the supplied people, products, interfaces, locations, and finite recorded actions rather than edit them. This task is scored on traceability to measured source ranges, final framing, and truthful use of separate audio, which a newly generated clip cannot satisfy.

doability_proof.status: doable with the current ChatGPT Adobe connector profile and declared exception paths
proof: Every required operation is present in the captured 99-tool ChatGPT Adobe inventory.
The client brief is host-neutral; connector-specific scoring is isolated in connector_profile and verifier_contract.
Artifact acceptance never depends on a raw connector response field.
Unsupported truth, fabrication, press, legal, or color claims have an explicit defer or disclose state.
residual_limits: Express work is template adaptation, not unrestricted canvas authoring.
Quick Cut is used only for visually led selection and never as semantic speech editing.
Automatic vectorization does not independently establish fabrication readiness.
Interactive Acrobat page-organization operations are excluded from zero-human execution.

acceptance_bar_note: The acceptance bar applies only to the scoped deliverables above. Hidden defects and connector quirks remain benchmark-internal and are not leaked into the client-facing brief.
